text.p: These are the leading stories in Pakistani newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Six people died and seven suffered serious burn wounds when a Pakistan Air Force Mirage fighter jettisoned two fuel tanks over the densely-populated area of Liaquatabad in Karachi on Thursday.
- Widespread and prolonged power breakdowns hit many parts of Karachi on Thursday.
- Army has been called out in several cities of Punjab province to help civil administration maintain law and order during the Moslem mourning month of Muharram, which starts on Friday.
- Three more drug pushers were sentenced to death by a court in Lahore on Thursday.

- The Pakistan army has agreed to spare troops for the supervision of the much delayed population census in the country, which the government plans to hold later this year, an official said on Thursday.
- Pakistan awarded contracts for the purchase of 330,000 tonnes of wheat worth $60 million to U.S. and Australian companies on Wednesday, triggering a price rise in the international wheat market.
- Pakistan's cash foreign exchange reserves, excluding gold reserves, slipped to $867.76 million on May 3, from $883.91 million a week ago.

- South Africa has urged the Indian Ocean Rim Association for Regional Cooperation to convene an emergency meeting to approve membership of developing countries in the region, including Pakistan, the South African High Commissioner in Pakistan said on Thursday.
- A delegation of Japanese businessmen is arriving in Pakistan on May 27 to seek investment opportunities.
THE NEWS
- Buyers of Pakistan's state enterprises and utilities will have to pay at least 60 percent of the price as first instalment in line with the new government policy to discourage defaulters.
- Troops were deployed in Jhang town of Punjab province on Thursday as a precautionary measure to avert any untoward incident during the Moslem mourning period of Muharram.

- Pakistan has lodged a strong complaint with the United States administration against the U.S. Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) for allegedly conducting a secret operation to trap Pakistani military officers in a DEA-financed under-cover operation, according to high-ranking officials.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has set up an eight-member committee to propose legal and constitutional reforms.
THE NATION

- A ban is likely to be imposed on all cash payments exceeding 25,000 rupees from the next budget in an attempt to document Pakistan's economy. A law will be enacted binding everybody to make larger payments through cheques only.
THE MUSLIM
- The government decided on Thursday to introduce a law within a week to crush militant sectarian groups with full force to normalise law and order situation.

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Ehstab (accountability) Cell has finalised another list of more than 120 "corrupt" bureaucrats of pay scales from 17 to 21 and is going to take strict actiona against them on different charges.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz told the National Assembly on Thursday that there would be no devaluation of the rupee but said the State (central) Bank of Pakistan would continue to adjust the rupee value to maintain its strength against other currencies.
- Minister for Water and Power Chaudhy Nisar Ali Khan told the Senate (upper house) on Thursday that all subsidies on electricity had been withdrawn.
--Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
